digest.top_line: RTOG 0848: adjuvant chemoRT missed OS overall (HR 0.96, P=.38) but N0 pts saw 5-yr OS 48.1% vs 28.6% (interaction P=.0063).
digest.tldr: Upper GI carried the day, and the RT read is entirely in the subgroup: modern QA'd 50.4 Gy/28 fx IMRT added nothing to gem-based chemo overall, but the treatment-by-nodal-status interaction (OS P=.0063, DFS P=.014) puts resected N0 pancreas back in play as the population worth testing. Grade 3 tox 38% vs 19%; hypothesis-generating, n=91.

sites.intro: Post-resection pancreas: the first adjuvant CXRT trial with mandatory pre-treatment RT credentialing, and its only positive signal is a nodal-status interaction on a failed primary.

studies.name: RTOG 0848
studies.tldr: OS primary missed (HR 0.96, 90% CI 0.79-1.18, P=.38 1-sided), but treatment-by-nodal-status interaction favored CXRT in N0 (P=.0063).
details: 🔍 Phase IIR/III two-step: step 2 randomized 354 pts post-resection, no progression after 5 cycles gem-based chemo, ±CXRT after cycle 6
📊 1° EP OS not met: median 2.6 vs 2.3 yr; 5-yr 23.1% vs 27.9% (CXRT)
📐 DFS trend favors CXRT: HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.65-1.03), P=.089
📐 Nodal-status interaction: OS P=.0063, DFS P=.014; forest-plot N-stage subgroup P-interaction .022

details.text: 📊 Node-negative subgroup (n=91), CXRT vs chemo alone

details: 🔍 RT was tightly QA'd: 50.4 Gy/28 fx to tumor bed, pancreatojejunostomy, regional nodes; real-time central review before start
🔍 81% IMRT, 19% 3D conformal; 88% got ≥50 Gy; 79% no interruptions; per-protocol/acceptable in 92% of treated pts
⚠️ 14% randomized to CXRT never received it (18 refusals); as-treated sensitivity HR 0.98 (90% CI 0.80-1.20), unchanged

details.text: ⚠️ Grade 3 toxicity higher with CXRT, grade 4/5 not
subdetails: GI disorders grade 3-5: 11% vs 2%; diarrhea 6% vs 1%

details: ⚠️ No pt received FOLFIRINOX/mFOLFIRINOX; backbone was gemcitabine ± erlotinib, now superseded
🔗 vs ESPAC-1: CXRT was detrimental there (1994-2000, split-course low-dose 2D, no QA); 0848 modernized dose, IMRT, and credentialing
🔗 vs RTOG 9704: post-hoc showed RT protocol deviation tracked with worse survival; 0848 pre-empted that with mandatory pre-treatment review
⚠️ Nodal subgroup is a treatment-by-covariate interaction in a trial whose 1° EP failed; n=91 N0 pts, 55 events
⚠️ Accrual took ~9 yr; final analysis triggered at 5-yr follow-up with 270 (not 316) OS events, power 72%

verdict.rationale: Primary OS endpoint missed; the positive read rests on a treatment-by-nodal-status interaction in 91 N0 pts, on a gemcitabine backbone no longer standard.
verdict.audience: Resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, R0/R1, no progression after 5 cycles adjuvant chemo

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is the nodal interaction: N0 pts (n=91) had median OS 3.9 vs 3.0 yr and 5-yr OS 48.1% vs 28.6% with CXRT, at 50.4 Gy/28 fx to bed plus regional nodes with mandatory pre-treatment central review. That combination of dose, target and QA is deliverable today, and it moves the adjuvant RT question from whether to whom.
studies.monday_clinic: In a resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma pt who is node-negative and progression-free after adjuvant chemo, this supports discussing adjuvant chemoradiation; it does not extend to node-positive pts, where no treatment effect was seen, nor to margin-positive disease.

primary_endpoint.name: Overall survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: 90% CI 0.79-1.18, one-sided P=.38; primary endpoint not met

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter randomized phase IIR/III, two-step. Step 1 was gemcitabine versus gemcitabine + erlotinib (reported previously); **step 2 randomly assigned 354 pts 1:1** after five cycles without progression to a sixth chemotherapy cycle **± CXRT**. Opened Nov 2009, step 2 closed Oct 2018, analyzed Dec 2023; median follow-up 2.2 yr overall and 7.4 yr among survivors.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Curative-intent resection of **pancreatic head** adenocarcinoma with operative note confirming gross total resection and documented microscopic margin status; body/tail excluded on the basis of RTOG 9704. Median age 63, 55% male, Zubrod 1 in 56%, pT3 in 81%. **74% node-positive**, 17% margin-positive, CA19-9 ≤90 in 96%.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Adjuvant backbone was gemcitabine (67%) or **gemcitabine + erlotinib** (28%), with 5% non-oxaliplatin gemcitabine combinations. **No patient received FOLFIRINOX or mFOLFIRINOX.** Radiosensitization was capecitabine in 83% and infusional 5-FU in 15%.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **50.4 Gy in 28 fractions** beginning within 21 days of cycle 6, targeting the postoperative tumor bed, pancreatojejunostomy and **regional nodes**. 81% IMRT, 19% 3D conformal; median delivered dose 50.4 Gy over 38 days, 88% received ≥50 Gy, 79% had no interruption. Planning underwent **real-time central review** before start at IROC-credentialed centers; overall per-protocol/acceptable in 92% of treated pts.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival** from second-step random assignment, powered for HR 0.76 at 80% with 316 events. Secondary: disease-free survival and CTCAE v4.0 adverse events.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **No excess grade 4/5 AEs** (6% v 5%, P=.68), but grade 3 rose to **38% v 19% (P<.001)**, driven by GI events (grade 3-5 GI 11% v 2%; diarrhea 6% v 1%) and lymphopenia (10% v 2%). One grade 5 event per arm (hepatic failure; sepsis). Discontinuation for toxicity was 5% on capecitabine and 17% on infusional 5-FU.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma progression-free through five cycles of gemcitabine-based adjuvant chemotherapy. Does not represent body/tail primaries, FOLFIRINOX-treated pts, or the neoadjuvant setting where nodal status after chemotherapy is harder to interpret.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: ESPAC-1 turned the field away from adjuvant chemoradiation, but it accrued 1994-2000 with split-course lower-dose 2D planning, no QA and no postoperative imaging to exclude early metastases. RTOG 9704's post-hoc analysis linked RT protocol deviations to worse survival; 0848 answered both with credentialed centers and mandatory pre-treatment review, and the chemotherapy-alone arm's outcomes track prior single-agent gemcitabine adjuvant trials.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The nodal finding is an interaction test, not a randomized comparison within N0, and rests on 91 pts with 55 OS events. Margin-positive disease cannot be addressed at all: **only 10 pts (5 per arm) were node-negative and margin-positive**. Accrual took nearly 9 years, and the analysis trigger changed to 5-year follow-up rather than 316 events, leaving 270 events and 72% power.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Codominant locoregional and systemic failure persists after resection, and the trial's own read is that a locoregional modality pays off only where the competing risk of distant failure is lower, which is what N0 status marks. The safety data are the least ambiguous result: modern CXRT costs grade 3 GI toxicity and lymphopenia, not grade 4/5 events.

studies.interpretation:
The honest headline is a negative trial: with 270 deaths, adding fluoropyrimidine-sensitized radiotherapy to a sixth cycle of gemcitabine-based adjuvant chemotherapy produced HR 0.96 for overall survival, and the as-treated sensitivity analysis moved it to 0.98. Nothing in the primary comparison supports routine adjuvant chemoradiation, and the investigators do not argue otherwise. What makes the trial worth reading anyway is that it was built to answer a question ESPAC-1 arguably never asked cleanly, and its most defensible contribution is not the survival curve but the demonstration that the modality can be delivered at scale without the harm the field assumed.

The ESPAC-1 comparison matters because that trial has functioned as the reason not to irradiate for two decades. Its radiotherapy was split-course, lower dose, 2D-planned, delivered without central quality assurance, in patients accrued before postoperative imaging routinely excluded incomplete resections and early metastatic disease. RTOG 9704 then supplied a mechanism for how such a trial could underperform: deviation from specified planning tracked with worse survival. RTOG 0848 removed those confounders deliberately, with credentialed centers, mandatory pre-treatment plan review, and 92% per-protocol or acceptable-variation delivery in treated patients. The result is that a negative OS result here carries more information than a negative result in ESPAC-1 did, because it is much harder to blame on technique. It also means the safety claim is the trial's most transferable finding: 6% versus 5% grade 4/5 events, with the excess confined to grade 3 gastrointestinal toxicity and lymphopenia, retires the argument that adjuvant chemoradiation in this setting is dangerous.

The node-negative signal deserves the caution its statistics demand and the attention its biology earns. It is an interaction test, not a randomized comparison within a prespecified stratum with its own alpha, and it rests on 91 patients and 55 events, with 5-year OS 48.1% versus 28.6%. Interactions of that kind are the single most common way a negative trial gets rescued into practice and then fails replication. But the mechanistic story is unusually coherent: local failure after resection runs in the 30% to 40% range, failure is codominantly locoregional and systemic, and a locoregional modality can only convert to survival where distant failure is not already the dominant competing risk. Node positivity marks exactly that competing risk, and 74% of this trial was node-positive. On that reading the overall null is what a diluted true effect looks like, not evidence of no effect anywhere.

The harder problem is generalization. Every patient received gemcitabine-based therapy and none received FOLFIRINOX, so the trial tests local therapy against a systemic backbone the field has moved past. That cuts both ways. A more effective systemic regimen reduces distant failure and could enlarge the population in whom local control translates into survival, which is the argument for a modern randomized test; or it could improve outcomes enough that the marginal contribution of radiotherapy shrinks. The trial cannot distinguish these, and it says so. Practically, the finding also does not survive transplantation into the neoadjuvant era intact, because post-chemotherapy nodal status is not the same variable as upfront nodal status. And margin-positive disease is untouched: with 10 node-negative, margin-positive patients total, the question that most often prompts a radiation referral is the one this trial cannot answer.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 50.4 Gy/28 fx to bed, pancreatojejunostomy and regional nodes, with mandatory pre-treatment central review, produced no excess grade 4/5 toxicity (6% v 5%) and 5-yr OS 48.1% v 28.6% in the N0 subgroup. The technique is reproducible today, so the adjuvant RT question becomes patient selection, not feasibility.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The backbone was gemcitabine ± erlotinib with zero FOLFIRINOX exposure, so the null OS result cannot be read as radiotherapy failing alongside current systemic therapy. Grade 3 AEs rose to 38% v 19%, mostly GI and lymphopenia, which is the cost to weigh when sequencing a sixth cycle plus CXRT.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Eligibility required gross total resection of a pancreatic head primary with documented microscopic margin status; body and tail were excluded. Node-negative pathology, not margin status, identified who benefited, and with only 10 node-negative margin-positive pts the trial says nothing about R1 resections.

papers.title: Adjuvant Chemotherapy ± Chemoradiotherapy for Adenocarcinoma of the Pancreatic Head: Results of the Radiotherapy Random Assignment of NRG Oncology/RTOG 0848
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To assess whether adding fluoropyrimidine sensitized radiotherapy (CXRT) to adjuvant chemotherapy improves overall survival (OS) after curative intent resection of the pancreatic head. METHODS This was a multicenter, randomized phase III, two step trial. Step 1: gemcitabine versus gemcitabine + erlotinib (previously reported). Step 2: random assignment to sixth chemotherapy cycle ± CXRT after five cycles of step 1 chemotherapy without progression. Outcomes of step 2 random assignment are reported here. Assuming 17 months median OS (chemotherapy alone), the sample size was 354 patients (hazard ratio [HR], 0.76, 80% power, one-sided α = .05, 316 OS events). OS/disease-free survival (DFS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier and arms compared using the log-rank test. RESULTS A total of 354 patients (median age 63, 55% male, 56% performance status, 1) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy (174) or chemotherapy + CXRT (180). Univariable median and 5-year OS (90% CIs) were 2.6 years (2.1-3.1) and 23.1% (17.7-28.6) for chemotherapy alone, and 2.3 years (2.0-2.6) and 27.9% (22.2-33.6) for chemotherapy + CXRT. The OS primary end point was not met (HR, 0.96 [90% CI, 0.79 to 1.18]; one-sided P = .38, two-sided P = .77). Chemotherapy + CXRT was associated with a trend for improved DFS (univariably; HR, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.65 to 1.03]; P = .089), without increase in grade 4/5 toxicities. However, grade 3 toxicity increased (38% v 19%, P < .001). Significantly, treatment by nodal status interactions showed that CXRT improved OS ( P = .0063) and DFS ( P = .014) in node-negative patients. CONCLUSION Overall, the addition of adjuvant CXRT to adjuvant gemcitabine did not statistically significantly improve OS, DFS, or increase grade 4/5 toxicity. For node-negative patients, CXRT improved OS and DFS. These results, if confirmed in studies with current or future systemic therapies, would support the use of adjuvant/neoadjuvant CXRT for node-negative patients.
